initiative.title: Release Cadence Query Recovery
initiative.summary: Prevent transient Git query failures from being misclassified as a clean release cadence no-op.

taskset.summary: Harden the cadence query boundary and prove release-auto fails loud on exhausted transient queries while preserving genuine no-tag behavior.

tasks.title: Recover transient non-zero cadence queries without false not-triggered
tasks.goal: Close GitHub issue 316 by preventing a valid tagged cadence from collapsing into release-auto not-triggered after a transient non-zero Git query result.
tasks.scope: Change only release-cadence Git query classification/retry behavior, its generated-host mirror, focused release cadence and release-auto regressions, and the host lock. Preserve cadence thresholds, bump policy, and the legitimate no-tag quiet path.
tasks.summary: Close GitHub issue 316 by distinguishing legitimate no-tag responses from transient non-zero Git query failures.
acceptance: One transient unexpected non-zero Git query result is retried and a subsequent valid cadence answer triggers normally.
Exhausted unexpected non-zero Git query results produce git-query-error diagnostics and release-auto trigger-error rather than not-triggered.
A repository with no tags remains a deterministic quiet pass.
Cadence thresholds, bump semantics, root/template parity, and the generated-host lock remain correct.

units.title: Classify and retry unexpected non-zero cadence queries
units.context: PR 315 CI run 29936269777 attempt 1 returned release-auto not-triggered for a valid v0.2.0 plus 40-commit fixture; the unchanged retry passed. TASK-AR-607 isolated dynamically loaded test module facades but intentionally left production query handling unchanged. release_cadence_trigger._git currently treats every positive non-zero return code as a deterministic empty answer, which can collapse a transient Git failure into no-tag or below-threshold state.
units.scope: Add failure-first query result classification and retry coverage, then distinguish the expected no-tag Git response from unexpected non-zero failures. Retry only the unexpected transient path, record exhausted diagnostics, mirror the runtime implementation, and regenerate the host lock.
steps: Reproduce one unexpected non-zero Git query result collapsing a valid tagged fixture into not-triggered.
Add a deterministic no-tag classifier and retry unexpected non-zero query results without changing thresholds.
Prove exhausted failures surface git-query-error through cadence and release-auto.
Mirror the implementation, regenerate the host lock, and run repeated focused probes plus the full matrix.
acceptance: A transient non-zero result followed by real Git output recovers without query errors.
Three unexpected non-zero results yield structured command, return code, and sanitized diagnostic evidence.
The known no-tag stderr remains a quiet no-baseline-tag result.
Root and generated-host implementations are byte-identical and all focused tests pass.
units.handoff: Report failure-first evidence, the non-zero/no-tag classification matrix, retry counts, structured diagnostics, focused and repeated test results, parity, host lock, and independent W4b review.
units.stop_condition: Stop if the fix requires weakening a release gate, changing cadence thresholds, or modifying unrelated status consumers.
